correctness.rationale: For positive homogeneous valuations of weights (1,1,1,rho), each directed individual inter-EF1 condition is x_i >= x_j−1 because each value per good is a positive constant. Thus all counts differ by at most one: m=4t+r has r large t+1 counts. Item-based realized-center EF1 is exactly a+b>=c+d−1 and c+rho*d>=a+b−1 (including empty centers). Let u be count of large bundles in A: 2u>=r−1, so least u=0 for r0,1 and u=1 for r2,3, which maximizes centre-B realized slack. Assign any large B bundle first to B1 (unit valuer); four extremal vectors r0(t,t,t,t), r1(t,t,t+1,t), r2(t+1,t,t+1,t), r3(t+1,t,t+1,t+1) have centre-B slack respectively 1−t(1−rho), 2−t(1−rho), 1−t(1−rho), 1−t+rho(t+1). These are necessary and sufficient for every m≥1; hence r0,2: t rho≥t−1; r1: t rho≥t−2; r3: (t+1)rho≥t−1. All m<=7 feasible, m8 impossible for rho<1/2, m9 always feasible, m10 again impossible for rho<1/2. Direct exhaustive count-vector enumeration m=1..16 across 60 rational rho settings reproduced the threshold formula; universal claim follows from the integer proof.

value.rationale: The same natural toy family used for an existing delegated-fairness impossibility theorem has a sharp residue-dependent feasibility classification over every item count and exceptional ratio. The first obstruction at eight and nonmonotonic recovery at nine are mathematically motivated, checkable and strictly more informative than a known twelve-good witness. Value is limited to this specific homogeneous-outlier family, which is stated honestly.

limitations: A fuller general multi-level fairness theorem under a matching valuation notion could imply part of the residue law, though Theorem 12 in the inspected same-model source uses potential rather than realized comparison.
